description:
I'm Youness zaarour a researcher in microwave and radar sensing based in Morocco, near Ben Guerir. I work on how radar signals interact with soil, water and materials.
For this project, we want to use NASA–ISRO NISAR radar data to reveal how Moroccan landscapes respond to the first autumn rains: soil moisture, vegetation and water, even when clouds hide the view. The goal is an interactive 3D experience that goes from the whole Earth down to a real place, with real satellite data and science.
summary: Dancing with the SARs turns NASA's new radar data into stories anyone can explore. Using the first public NISAR data (NASA-ISRO), NASA OPERA Sentinel-1 products and NASA POWER, our interactive web app tracks three kinds of surface change in Morocco: soil moisture through the dry summer and the first autumn rains around Ben Guerir, ground motion around the Ben Guerir phosphate mine (NISAR interferograms), and ten years of construction in Casablanca (Sentinel-1 radar 2016-2026, checked against an independent settlement map, F1 0.80). A 3D Earth shows NISAR, Sentinel-1 and SWOT in orbit; a map of Morocco's 12 regions lets anyone click a place and get its weather and soil from NASA POWER, NISAR radar values and soil moisture near the region capitals, and the latest radar passes, read live from NASA's catalogue. A live page lists new NISAR and Sentinel-1 acquisitions worldwide, and an import tool reads your own zone, field measurements or NISAR soil-moisture file in the browser. Every value is labelled as NISAR data, derived, our interpretation or simulated, so users see what radar can and cannot tell them. It matters because radar sees the ground through clouds, day and night, but its data is hard to read: we make it understandable for farmers, planners and students.
details:
What it does. Dancing with the SARs is an interactive web app that turns NASA radar data into stories about how Morocco's land changes. A 3D Earth shows NISAR, Sentinel-1 and SWOT on their orbits and leads to four radar stories:

  1. Water and moisture: NISAR L3 soil moisture (DSG algorithm) around Ben Guerir through the dry summer and the first autumn rains, compared with NASA POWER rain.
  2. Ground motion: NISAR L2 interferograms (GUNW) around the Ben Guerir phosphate mine, measured against a stable reference ring.
  3. Soil and vegetation signals: NISAR backscatter (HH, HV) and its changes between passes.
  4. Construction growth: settlement maps 1985-2019 (DLR WSF) and Sentinel-1 radar 2016-2026 (NASA OPERA RTC-S1). Casablanca's radar map matches the independent 2019 settlement map at F1 0.80. For Ben Guerir, a small low-rise town, the match is only 0.35, so we show its radar images but no area figures.

A Findings page states what we conclude and the limits of the data.

Interactive tools. A map of Morocco's 12 regions: click any place and get its weather and soil from NASA POWER (latest day, 30-day chart, comparison with the 2001-2025 normal), NISAR radar values and soil moisture near the region capitals, and the latest NISAR and Sentinel-1 passes. A Live radar page lists new NISAR and Sentinel-1 acquisitions worldwide, read live from NASA's Common Metadata Repository. An import tool reads your own zone (GeoJSON/KML), field measurements (CSV) or a NISAR soil-moisture file (.h5) directly in the browser.

How it works. Python tools read NASA products from ASF DAAC, downloading only the window needed (HTTP byte ranges), compute the time series and pass a publish check (no missing values, rejected passes listed). The site is a static React + three.js app; live data (NASA CMR, NASA POWER) are read directly in the browser, with no server.

Benefits and impact. Radar sees the ground through clouds, day and night, but its data is hard to read. We make it understandable, in plain language and for any place in Morocco, for farmers, planners, students and local authorities, without downloading data or learning radar processing.

What makes it creative. One continuous journey from orbit to a single field; real 3D satellites you can click; before/after sliders on real radar images; a live worldwide feed; and every value labelled "NISAR data", "derived from NISAR", "our interpretation" or "simulated, demo only", so users see what radar can and cannot say.

What we considered. Scientific honesty first: provisional NISAR products are marked PROVISIONAL, a bad pass (7 Sep) is rejected and listed, one soil-moisture algorithm is used throughout, and results that do not pass validation (Ben Guerir construction) are not shown as numbers. Also speed on phones, accessibility, and Morocco's borders (Morocco point-of-view map).

Tools. Python (numpy, scipy, h5py, tifffile, pyproj, Pillow), React 19, TypeScript, Vite, three.js and React Three Fiber, GSAP, h5wasm, Autodesk Fusion 360 (satellite models), Git and Vercel.

Use of AI. Claude (Anthropic) helped write code, process data and draft text; the video voice-over is an ElevenLabs synthetic voice; the four story card pictures are AI-generated illustrations, marked "Illustration (AI-generated), not data" on the site. All data, numbers and sources were checked against the original NASA products.
